title: Enhancing solar desalination efficiency: Performance analysis of coated hemi‐cylindrical solar stills
content:
Abstract

The intention of the present investigation was to experimentally enhance the effectiveness of hemi-cylindrical solar stills (HCSS). The current article imparts an extensive energy and exergy analysis of both a typical SS and one with Chlorinated polyvinyl chloride (CPVC), N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) coated modified HCSS. This investigation is novel as it examines the coated HCSS that yields more water. The findings revealed that a rise of 15% in clean water production occurs after the coatings were applied to the HCSS. The conventional HCSS and coated HCSS have the highest yield productivity of 1.985 and 2.87 L/m2, respectively. An improvement in the distillate yield per day of 0.455 L/m2 on 19th May 2025, 0.45 L/m2 on 20th May 2025, 0.445 L/m2 on 21st May 2025, 0.41 L/m2 on 22nd May 2025, 0.51 L/m2 on 23rd May 2025, 0.445 L/m2 on 24th May 2025, for a 1.5 mm coated HCSS. 260 W of output power was obtained for conventional SS, while a coated HCSS achieved 297 W of output power. The conventional HCSS has energy and exergy efficacies of 7.2% and 0.7%, respectively, whereas the coated HCSS has energy and exergy efficacies of 27.4% and 4.2%.
